s: An outbreak of which of the following led to the first session of the INC (1885) being shifted from Poona to Bombay?
x: The shift was due to cholera, not plague; the session met at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, under Viceroy Dufferin.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Lord Ripon — Influence on Hume's interest in local self-government
A.O. Hume — Father of Indian Ornithology
A.O. Hume — First General Secretary of the INC
Lord Lytton — Initial encouragement of Hume's annual forum idea
x: Lord Dufferin, not Lord Lytton, initially encouraged Hume's idea of an annual forum. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: To whom is the name 'Indian National Congress' credited?
x: The name is credited to Dadabhai Naoroji; Bonnerjee presided over the first session, and Hume's Indian (National) Union was one of its organisational origins.

s: Lord Dufferin, after first tolerating the Congress, later dismissed it as representing which kind of minority?
x: Dufferin first showed official tolerance but later criticised the Congress as representing a 'microscopic minority'.

s: The delegates to the first session of the Indian National Congress were drawn mainly from which occupational groups?
x: Most delegates were lawyers, journalists and teachers.

s: Which of the following is correct about Lord Dufferin's role in the formation of the INC?
o: Founded it by an official proclamation in 1885
Opposed every proposal for a forum of educated Indians
Probably suggested an annual meeting of educated Indians, but did not demonstrably propose the INC
x: Dufferin may have suggested an annual forum of educated Indians, but there is no proof that he proposed the INC itself.

s: Which Theosophical Convention was followed by the private meeting of 17 people that led to the INC?
x: The meeting of 17 people came after the Theosophical Convention at Madras in December 1884.

s: Where in Bombay was the first INC session (28-31 December 1885) held?
x: The first session met at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Indian National Congress was founded during the viceroyalty of Lord Dufferin.
2. Lord Dufferin mocked the Congress as a 'microscopic minority' in 1888.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Dufferin (1884-88) was Viceroy when the INC was founded in 1885, and in 1888 he dismissed it as a 'microscopic minority'.

s: Where was the first session of the INC (1885) held?
o: Gokul Das Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay
x: The first INC session met at Gokul Das Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, on 28-30 December 1885.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tyabji — first Muslim president of the INC, 1887
George Yule — first woman president of the INC, 1888
Annie Besant — first English president of the INC, 1917
P. Anandacharlu — first Muslim president of the INC, 1891
x: Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim president of the INC in 1887. George Yule was the first English president in 1888, and Annie Besant was the first woman president in 1917.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Badruddin Tyabji presided over the 1887 Madras session.
Rahimtulla M. Sayani was associated with the 1896 Calcutta session.
Rahimtulla M. Sayani was the first Muslim President of the INC.
Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim President of the INC.
x: Option C is incorrect: Rahimtulla M. Sayani, who presided at Calcutta in 1896, was the second Muslim President. Badruddin Tyabji, President at Madras in 1887, was the first.

s: Who was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress?
x: Sarojini Naidu (Kanpur 1925) was the first Indian woman President; Annie Besant (Calcutta 1917) was the first woman President, and Nellie Sengupta presided at Calcutta in 1933.

s: In which year did Gandhi give up his primary membership of the Congress?
x: Gandhi resigned in 1934 and never formally rejoined, though he remained its guiding leader.

s: Which was the only INC session presided over by Mahatma Gandhi?
x: Gandhi presided over the INC only once, at Belgaum in 1924, where he reconciled the Swarajists and No-Changers.

s: At which session did Abul Kalam Azad become the youngest President of the INC, at the age of 35?
x: Azad presided over the special Delhi session of 1923 at 35, the youngest INC President.

s: Which leader presided over the Indian National Congress three times and is remembered as the Grand Old Man of India?
x: Dadabhai Naoroji, the Grand Old Man of India, presided three times - Calcutta 1886, Lahore 1893 and Calcutta 1906 (APPSC-GS 2025). Bonnerjee (1885, 1892) and Surendranath Banerjee (1895, 1902) presided twice each; Pherozeshah Mehta, the Lion of Bombay, once (1890).

s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: W.C. Bonnerjee — Grand Old Man of India
x: Pherozeshah Mehta was known as the “Lion of Bombay.” Dadabhai Naoroji was the “Grand Old Man of India,” and Surendranath Banerjee was known as “Rashtraguru.”

s: In which years did W.C. Bonnerjee preside over the INC?
x: Bonnerjee presided twice, in 1885 (Bombay) and 1892 (Allahabad).

s: How many times did Dadabhai Naoroji preside over the Indian National Congress?
x: Naoroji presided three times; Surendranath Banerjee and Rash Behari Ghosh presided twice each and Pherozeshah Mehta once.

s: Who is known as the 'Lion of Bombay'?
x: Pherozeshah Mehta, INC president in 1890, was called the Lion of Bombay.

s: About how many delegates attended the second INC session at Calcutta in 1886?
x: The 1886 Calcutta session had 436 delegates, against 72 at the first session.

s: Kadambini Ganguly, who addressed the 1890 Calcutta session of the INC, was the first woman graduate of which university?
x: Kadambini Ganguly was Calcutta University's first woman graduate and addressed the 1890 session presided over by Pherozeshah Mehta.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: P. Anandacharlu presided over the Nagpur session of 1891, the seventh session. Sayani presided in 1896, Dinshaw Wacha in 1901, and Naoroji in Lahore in 1893.

s: Who presided over the Lucknow session of the INC in 1916?
x: Ambica Charan Mazumdar presided at Lucknow in 1916; R.C. Dutt presided at Lucknow in 1899 and Bonnerjee at Allahabad in 1892.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Rash Behari Ghosh – Poona 1895 and Ahmedabad 1902
x: Pherozeshah Mehta presided at Calcutta in 1890; Surendranath Banerjee at Poona 1895 and Ahmedabad 1902; Rash Behari Ghosh at Surat 1907 and Madras 1908.

s: At which session did the Extremists re-enter the Congress after the Surat split of 1907?
x: Surat split the Congress and the Extremists re-entered at Lucknow in 1916; Calcutta 1906 had adopted Swaraj as the goal.

s: Who presided over the Surat session of the INC in 1907?
x: Rash Behari Ghosh presided at Surat in 1907; Gokhale at Benares 1905 and Mazumdar at Lucknow 1916.

s: Who presided over the Madras session of the INC in 1894?
x: Alfred Webb presided at Madras in 1894; Naoroji at Calcutta 1886, Sayani at Calcutta 1896 and Gokhale at Benares 1905.

s: At which session was Swaraj declared the goal of the INC under Dadabhai Naoroji?
x: Calcutta 1906 declared Swaraj the goal under Naoroji; Benares 1905 was presided over by Gokhale and Surat 1907 saw the split.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Lucknow Pact was in 1916; Swaraj was adopted in 1906, the Surat Split came in 1907 and the Nehru Report in 1928.

s: Who presided over the Bombay session of the INC in 1889?
x: William Wedderburn presided at Bombay in 1889.

s: Which session of the Indian National Congress saw the Moderate–Extremist split?
x: Surat 1907 saw the split; Lucknow 1916 brought the Lucknow Pact and the Extremists' return, and Nagpur 1920 adopted Non-Cooperation.

s: Who presided over the Madras session of the INC in 1898?
x: A.M. Bose presided at Madras in 1898; Webb in 1894, Ghosh in 1908 and Basu in 1914.

s: Who presided over the Madras session of the INC in 1914?
x: The 1914 Madras session was presided over by Bhupendranath Basu.

s: After the Lahore session of 1929 adopted Purna Swaraj, which day was observed as Independence Day?
x: Following the Lahore resolution under Jawaharlal Nehru, 26 January 1930 was observed as Independence Day.

s: Which of the following pairs (INC President – session) is correctly matched?
x: Vallabhbhai Patel presided at Karachi in 1931; Motilal Nehru at Calcutta 1928, Jawaharlal Nehru at Lahore 1929 and Bose at Haripura 1938.

s: Which event provided the context preceding the Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress in 1931?
x: The Gandhi–Irwin Pact of March 1931 suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement, and the Karachi Session that month endorsed it. The Lucknow Pact, Surat Split and Nehru Report belong to earlier years.

s: Who presided over the Nagpur session of the INC in 1920?
x: C. Vijayaraghavachariar presided at Nagpur in 1920; Motilal Nehru at Amritsar 1919, C.R. Das at Gaya 1922 and Gandhi at Belgaum 1924.

s: Which was the first rural session of the Indian National Congress?
x: Faizpur (December 1936) was the first rural session; Karachi 1931 adopted the Fundamental Rights resolution and Nehru presided at Lucknow in April 1936.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Jaipur Session of the Indian National Congress is incorrect?
o: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the session.
It was the 55th Session of the INC.
J.B. Kripalani presided over the session.
x: Option D is incorrect: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the 55th session at Jaipur in December 1948. J.B. Kripalani was President in 1946–47.

s:
Arrange the following INC sessions in chronological order:
A. 1928 Calcutta
B. 1931 Karachi
C. 1929 Lahore
D. 1936 Faizpur
x: Calcutta was held in 1928, Lahore in 1929, Karachi in 1931 and Faizpur in 1936, giving the order A, C, B, D.

s: Which session of the INC debated the Nehru Report?
x: Calcutta 1928 debated the Nehru Report; Kanpur 1925 had Sarojini Naidu as the first Indian woman President and Ramgarh 1940 had Azad.

s:
Assertion (A): Subhas Chandra Bose was re-elected as INC President in 1939.
Reason (R): Subhas Chandra Bose later resigned as INC President.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Bose was re-elected at Tripuri in 1939 by defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya, and he resigned later that year. A later resignation cannot cause an earlier re-election.

s: Who presided over the last INC session before independence?
x: J.B. Kripalani presided over the Meerut session of November 1946, the last before Independence. Azad was President from 1940 to 1946, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided after Independence, in 1948.

s: The formation of the National Planning Committee was associated with which Indian National Congress session?
x: The National Planning Committee was set up in 1938, after the Haripura session, under Congress President Subhas Chandra Bose, with Nehru as Chairman.

s: With whom was the Nehru Report associated?
x: Motilal Nehru chaired the Nehru Report committee; Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Purna Swaraj resolution at Lahore.

s: What was the consequence mentioned in connection with the 1928 Calcutta Session if the Nehru Report was not accepted within the year?
o: A mass movement would be launched
Purna Swaraj Day would be observed
The national flag would be hoisted on the Ravi
The Congress–League Agreement would be concluded
x: The 1928 Calcutta Session gave the British one year to accept the Nehru Report; otherwise the Congress would launch a mass movement. When the year passed, this led to Purna Swaraj and Civil Disobedience.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Nehru Report came in 1928; the Congress–League pact was in 1916, the Purna Swaraj Resolution in 1929 and Purna Swaraj Day on 26 January 1930.

s: Who presided over the 1927 Madras session of the INC, associated with the boycott of the Simon Commission?
x: The 1927 session met at Madras under M.A. Ansari.

s: At which INC session was the resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme adopted?
x: The Karachi session (1931) under Patel adopted the Fundamental Rights resolution.

s: Who presided over the Calcutta session of the INC in 1933?
x: Nellie Sengupta presided over the 1933 Calcutta session.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the Tripuri Session is incorrect?
o: The internal conflict resulted in the continuation of Bose as Congress President without resignation.
Subhas Chandra Bose was re-elected President.
It was associated with an internal conflict.
x: Option A is incorrect: Bose was re-elected at Tripuri in 1939, but opposition from the Gandhian group forced him to resign; he then formed the Forward Bloc. The other statements are right.

s: Who presided over the Jaipur session of the INC in 1948?
x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided at Jaipur in 1948; Nehru at Faizpur 1936, Bose at Tripuri 1939 and Azad at Ramgarh 1940.

s: Which party did C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru form after the 1922 Gaya session of the INC rejected council entry?
x: The Gaya session (1922) rejected council entry, after which C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party.

s: Who presided over the 1931 Karachi session of the INC?
x: Patel presided at Karachi in 1931; Nehru presided at Lahore 1929 and Faizpur 1936, and Bose at Haripura 1938.

s: Whom did Subhas Chandra Bose defeat to be re-elected President of the INC at Tripuri in 1939?
x: At Tripuri (1939) Bose was re-elected by defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya, but soon resigned.

s: Which party did Subhas Chandra Bose form after resigning as INC President in 1939?
x: After resigning the Congress presidency in 1939, Bose formed the Forward Bloc.

s: Which INC session was the last session attended by Tilak?
x: The Amritsar session of 1919 was Tilak's last; he died in 1920.

s: Who presided over the Amritsar session of the INC in 1919?
x: Motilal Nehru presided over the Amritsar session of 1919.

s: Who was the chairman of the National Planning Committee set up at the time of the Haripura session (1938)?
x: Bose presided at Haripura, and the National Planning Committee was set up with Nehru as chairman.

s: Who presided over the Gaya session of the INC in 1922?
x: C.R. Das presided at Gaya in 1922; Sarojini Naidu at Kanpur 1925, Mudholkar at Bankipore 1912 and Azad at Ramgarh 1940.

s: Who presided over the Kakinada session of the INC in 1923?
x: Maulana Mohammad Ali presided at Kakinada in 1923; Rash Behari Ghosh (1908), Bhupendranath Basu (1914) and M.A. Ansari (1927) presided at Madras.

s: On which date did T. Prakasam start the English daily Swarajya to spread the Congress message?
x: Prakasam started Swarajya on 26 October 1921.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Nyapati Subba Rao was the first President of the Andhra Congress Circle.
The ban on the Hyderabad State Congress was lifted in 1946.
The Kurnool Circular was issued by State Congress leaders during the Civil Disobedience Movement.
Govinda Rao Nanal was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Kurnool (Andhra) Circular was issued during the Quit India Movement of 1942, not Civil Disobedience. A, B and D are right.

s: Who started the paper Swarajya?
x: T. Prakasam started Swarajya; Pattabhi Sitaramaiah wrote the History of the Indian National Congress.

s: Which one of the following sets contains only Andhra delegates to the first session of the Indian National Congress?
o: P. Anandacharlu, P. Rangaiah Naidu, Nyapathi Subbarao, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu
P. Anandacharlu, Dadabhai Naoroji, Nyapathi Subbarao, George Yule and Venkata Subbarayudu
P. Rangaiah Naidu, William Wedderburn, Gutti Kesava Pillai, Pherozeshah Mehta and Nyapathi Subbarao
Nyapathi Subbarao, W.C. Bonnerjee, P. Anandacharlu, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Dinshaw Wacha
x: The Andhra delegates listed were P. Anandacharlu, P. Rangaiah Naidu, Nyapathi Subbarao, Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu.

s: At which session did Ponaka Kanakamma, the first Telugu woman to attend an INC session, lead the women's wing?
x: She led the women's wing at the Kakinada (Coconada) session of 1923, not Madras 1914.

s: At the Madras session of the Indian National Congress in 1914, which of the following developments strengthened the demand for a separate Andhra Congress circle?
o: The adoption of a resolution creating a separate Andhra province
The participation of 256 Andhra delegates without any seat on the Working Committee
The election of an Andhra delegate as Congress President
The withdrawal of all Andhra delegates from the session
x: Although 256 Andhra delegates attended the Madras session in 1914, none obtained a Working Committee seat. This strengthened the demand for a separate Andhra Congress circle.

s: Which party broke continuous Congress rule in Andhra Pradesh in 1983?
x: In 1983 the TDP ended continuous Congress rule in Andhra Pradesh; Congress(I) had been formed on 1 January 1978.

s: With which movement is the Kurnool Circular associated?
x: The Kurnool Circular belongs to the Quit India Movement of 1942, not Civil Disobedience.

s: Who designed the tricolour that Gandhi hoisted at the Bezawada AICC meeting of 1921?
x: At Bezawada (31 March-1 April 1921) Gandhi hoisted Pingali Venkayya's tricolour.

s: At which session did P. Anandacharlu, the first Andhra President of the INC, preside?
x: Anandacharlu, a Chittoor delegate at the first session, presided at Nagpur in 1891; Kakinada 1923 was presided over by Maulana Mohammad Ali.

s: Which book was written by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramaiah?
o: History of the Indian National Congress
Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
x: Pattabhi Sitaramaiah wrote the History of the Indian National Congress; India's Struggle for Independence is by Bipan Chandra.

s: Who was the first president of the Hyderabad State Congress?
x: Govinda Rao Nanal was the first president of the Hyderabad State Congress, whose ban was lifted in 1946.

s: Who was the first president of the Andhra Congress circle?
x: After 256 Andhra delegates got no Working Committee seat at Madras 1914, a separate Andhra Congress circle was formed with Nyapati Subba Rao as its first president.

s: When did Indira Gandhi form the Congress (I)?
x: Indira Gandhi formed the Congress (I) on 1 January 1978.

s: By what title is A.O. Hume popularly known?
x: A.O. Hume is known as the Father of Indian Ornithology, in addition to his political role in the formation of the INC.

s: Which post did A.O. Hume, closer to the Bombay and Poona groups than to the Calcutta leaders, first hold in the INC?
x: Hume was closer to the Bombay and Poona groups and served as the first General Secretary of the INC.

s: After a clash with which Viceroy was A.O. Hume demoted in 1879?
x: Hume clashed with Lytton and was demoted in 1879; he retired in 1882 to Shimla and drew the idea of local self-government from Ripon.

s: Where did A.O. Hume settle after retiring in 1882?
x: Hume was demoted in 1879, retired in 1882 and settled at Shimla.

s: Which body did A.O. Hume form before the INC?
x: Hume formed the Indian (National) Union, which became the INC.

s: How is Hume seen in the 'lightning-conductor' interpretation of the Congress's origin?
o: Creating an outlet for popular discontent
Suppressing the Congress on Dufferin's orders
Shielding the young organisation from official hostility
x: The lightning-conductor view sees Hume shielding the infant Congress from official suppression, whereas the safety-valve view sees it as an outlet for discontent.

s: Who wrote the 1913 biography of A.O. Hume in which the safety-valve theory was first mentioned?
x: Wedderburn's 1913 biography first mentioned it; Lala Lajpat Rai then used it in Young India (1916) to attack the Moderates.

s: Who called the safety-valve theory a 'colonial myth' and described Hume's role as a 'lightning conductor'?
x: Bipan Chandra used both expressions; R.P. Dutt saw the Congress as a conspiracy to head off a popular uprising.

s: Who was the first to use the safety-valve theory, in Young India (1916)?
x: Wedderburn first mentioned it (1913), but Lajpat Rai first used it in Young India (1916) against the Moderates.

s: With whom is the Marxist 'conspiracy theory' of the INC's origin associated?
x: R.P. Dutt held that the INC was created to head off a popular uprising.

s: In which year did Hume read at Simla the secret reports on which the safety-valve theory rests?
x: Hume reportedly read seven volumes of secret reports at Simla in 1878.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the initial objectives of the Indian National Congress is incorrect?
o: It initially arranged for social issues to be raised from the Congress platform.
It aimed to remove caste, sectarian and regional biases.
It sought to formulate public demands.
x: Option A is incorrect: in its early years the Congress deliberately kept social reform issues off its platform to avoid division. National unity, removing caste, sectarian and regional biases, and formulating public demands were genuine early aims.

s: Which of the following was an early demand of the Indian National Congress?
o: Separation of the Executive and Judiciary
x: Separation of the Executive from the Judiciary was among the early Moderate demands, and formulating public demands was a founding objective.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the demands of the first session of the Indian National Congress?
o: Simultaneous ICS examinations in England and India
Immediate establishment of complete provincial autonomy
Opposition to the annexation of Upper Burma
Election in place of nomination for councils
x: The first session demanded simultaneous ICS examinations, elected councils, opposition to the annexation of Upper Burma and reduction of military expenditure. Immediate complete provincial autonomy was not listed among its four demands.

s:
Consider the following statements about the early Indian National Congress:
1. It provided the first all-India political platform.
2. It was initially a mass peasant organisation with a rural membership.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The early INC was the first all-India political platform, but its base was narrow, urban and educated, not rural peasant.

s: Who founded the Servants of India Society at Poona in 1905?
x: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society at Poona in 1905.

s: Who was Gopal Krishna Gokhale’s own guru?
x: M.G. Ranade was Gokhale’s political and intellectual guru.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Surendranath Banerjee – Servants of India Society
Gopal Krishna Gokhale – Servants of India Society
x: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society. Naoroji gave the Drain Theory, Banerjee founded the Indian National Association and R.C. Dutt wrote an economic critique of colonialism.

s: The Servants of India Society was founded at which place and on which date?
x: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society at Poona on 12 June 1905.

s: What was the aim of the Servants of India Society?
o: Train national workers by constitutional means
Lobby the British Parliament from London
x: Gokhale's Society trained national workers for India's service by constitutional means.

s: On whose advice did Gandhi return to India in 1915?
x: Gandhi came back in 1915 on Gokhale, his political guru's, advice.

s:
Assertion (A): Gopal Krishna Gokhale was called the Political Guru of Gandhi.
Reason (R): Gandhi himself acknowledged Gokhale as his political mentor and followed his advice to tour India after returning in 1915.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Both are true and R explains A: Gandhi openly called Gokhale his political guru and, on his advice, spent a year touring India after 1915, which is why Gokhale bears that title.

s: At which Congress session did Swaraj become the goal under Dadabhai Naoroji’s presidency?
x: Swaraj became the goal at the Calcutta Congress session of 1906 presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji.

s: In which years did Dadabhai Naoroji preside over the INC?
x: Naoroji presided three times: Calcutta 1886, Lahore 1893 and Calcutta 1906.

s: Dadabhai Naoroji served on which commission appointed in 1895?
x: Naoroji served on the Welby Commission (1895) on Indian expenditure.

s: In which year did Dadabhai Naoroji preside over the INC session at Lahore?
x: Naoroji presided at Calcutta in 1886, Lahore in 1893 and Calcutta again in 1906.

s: On which party's ticket was Dadabhai Naoroji elected to the House of Commons in 1892?
x: Naoroji won Central Finsbury in 1892 as a Liberal, becoming the first Indian member of the British Parliament.

s: Who was the first Indian to contest an election to the British House of Commons, in 1885?
x: Lal Mohan Ghose contested first (1885); Naoroji was the first Indian elected (1892).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Lal Mohan Ghose was the first Indian to contest an election to the House of Commons.
2. Dadabhai Naoroji was the first Indian to be elected to the House of Commons.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Lal Mohan Ghose contested in 1885; Naoroji was elected from Central Finsbury in 1892.

s: Who said that Britain was 'bleeding India white'?
x: Naoroji, author of the drain theory, said Britain was bleeding India white.

s: Who founded the London Indian Society in 1865 along with Dadabhai Naoroji?
x: Naoroji and W.C. Bonnerjee formed the London Indian Society in 1865, a year before the East India Association.

s: In which year was Dadabhai Naoroji elected to the British Parliament from Finsbury Central?
x: Naoroji became the first Indian elected to the British Parliament in 1892.

s: Who is the author of 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'?
x: Dadabhai Naoroji wrote Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (1901), which set out the drain theory.

s: From which constituency was Dadabhai Naoroji elected to the House of Commons in 1892?
x: Naoroji won Finsbury Central in 1892 as a Liberal, becoming the first Indian MP.

s: Which of the following is regarded as the greatest contribution of the Moderates to the Indian national movement?
o: The launch of mass civil disobedience
The demand for immediate complete independence
The organisation of armed revolutionary activities
x: The economic critique of colonialism was the greatest contribution of the Moderates. It exposed the exploitative character of British rule and destroyed the myth of British benevolence.

s: What did R.C. Dutt's economic critique argue?
o: Wealth holders should treat wealth as a social trust
Colonial policies caused India's economic exploitation
Truth-force was the only path to freedom
Self-government was the immediate nationalist goal
x: R.C. Dutt showed that colonial policies caused the economic exploitation of India.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Essays on Indian Economics — M.G. Ranade
Economic History of India — Bipan Chandra
Some Economic Aspects of British Rule in India — R.C. Dutt
The Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India — G. Subramania Iyer
x: M.G. Ranade wrote *Essays on Indian Economics*. The other works were authored by R.C. Dutt, G. Subramania Iyer and Bipan Chandra respectively.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: The Doctrine of Lapse is Lord Dalhousie's. The Drain Theory is Dadabhai Naoroji's, the Two-Nation Theory is linked with Jinnah and the Muslim League, and Hindutva with V.D. Savarkar.

s: How did the 'Safety Valve Theory' view the Indian National Congress?
o: A means of channelling political discontent
x: The Safety Valve Theory saw the INC as an outlet for channelling political discontent.

s: What did 'Swaraj' mean as a nationalist objective?
x: Swaraj meant political self-government as a nationalist objective.

s: Home Charges, salaries and pensions, and unequal trade were channels of which of the following?
x: The drain of India's wealth to Britain operated through Home Charges, salaries and pensions, unequal trade and British monopoly.

s: According to the Drain Theory, to which country was India's wealth being transferred?
x: The Drain Theory, an economic critique of colonialism, held that India's wealth was being drained to Britain.

s: Who wrote 'Economic History of India'?
x: Economic History of India is by R.C. Dutt, not R.P. Dutt.

s: Who wrote 'The Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India' (1966)?
x: Bipan Chandra wrote this 1966 study.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Essays on Indian Economics – R.C. Dutt
Economic History of India – Dadabhai Naoroji
Some Economic Aspects of British Rule in India – G. Subramania Iyer
Poverty and Un-British Rule in India – M.G. Ranade
x: Some Economic Aspects is by G. Subramania Iyer; Essays is Ranade's, Economic History is R.C. Dutt's and Poverty is Naoroji's.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
x: Trusteeship is Gandhi's idea, not Savarkar's.

s: What was the principal contribution of the early nationalists to the freedom movement?
o: organisation of armed revolution throughout India
economic critique of colonialism, especially the drain theory
x: The early nationalists made a major contribution by developing an economic critique of colonial rule, particularly the drain theory.

s: Who is regarded as the founder of the Indian National Congress?
x: A.O. Hume is treated as the founder of the INC; Naoroji was a founding figure and Wacha was not the founder.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the founding of the INC?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji presided over its 1885 session
A.O. Hume is regarded as its founder
W.C. Bonnerjee was its first President
Its first session was held at Bombay
x: The 1885 Bombay session was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee; Naoroji presided first in 1886.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: R.C. Dutt — *Rise of the Maratha Power*
x: Surendranath Banerjee wrote *A Nation in Making*. *The Bengalee* was associated with Banerjee, *Rise of the Maratha Power* with Ranade, and *Economic History of India* with R.C. Dutt.

s: With which of the following was the judge, economist and social reformer M.G. Ranade associated?
x: M.G. Ranade was associated with the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha; the other options belong to G. Subramania Iyer, R.C. Dutt and W.C. Bonnerjee.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji was associated with the Drain Theory.
Pherozeshah Mehta was associated with moderate nationalism and Bombay.
Gopal Krishna Gokhale was associated with Prarthana Samaj.
Surendranath Banerjee was associated with the Indian National Association.
x: Option C is incorrect: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society; the Prarthana Samaj is linked with M.G. Ranade. Naoroji's Drain Theory, Mehta in Bombay and Banerjee's Indian Association are right.

s: G. Subramania Iyer was associated with the founding of which pair of newspapers?
x: G. Subramania Iyer founded *The Hindu* and *Swadesamitran* and was associated with the Madras Mahajana Sabha.

s:
Consider the following statements about Pherozeshah Mehta:
1. He was known as the 'Lion of Bombay'.
2. He founded the Bombay Presidency Association in 1885.
3. He presided over the Lucknow session of 1899.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct; Mehta presided in 1890, while Lucknow 1899 was presided over by R.C. Dutt.

s: Who wrote 'Rise of the Maratha Power'?
x: M.G. Ranade wrote Rise of the Maratha Power and Essays on Indian Economics.

s: Which early Congress leader said 'no taxation without representation'?
x: The phrase is credited to Madan Mohan Malaviya.

s: Which INC session was presided over by Dinshaw Wacha?
x: Dinshaw Wacha presided at Calcutta in 1901.

s: Who was the first President of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
x: W.C. Bonnerjee presided over the first INC session at Bombay in 1885. Dadabhai Naoroji presided in 1886.

s: Who wrote 'A Nation in Making'?
x: A Nation in Making is the work of Surendranath Banerjee (Rashtraguru).

s: Who presided over the Lucknow session of the INC in 1899?
x: R.C. Dutt, the economic historian, presided over the Lucknow session of 1899.

s: With which of the following reform bodies was M.G. Ranade associated?
x: Ranade was associated with the Prarthana Samaj and the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha; Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society.

s: Whose deportation without trial did the Moderates protest against?
x: The Moderates protested against Tilak's arrest and the deportation of the Natu brothers without trial.

s: Which of the following was NOT a major economic demand of the Moderates?
x: The Moderates demanded cuts in military expenditure, along with lower land revenue, abolition of the salt tax and tariff protection for Indian industries.

s: Which one of the following was a constitutional demand of the Moderates?
o: Immediate establishment of a republican government
Larger councils with elected members and control over the budget
Replacement of the civil services by elected village bodies
x: The Moderates demanded larger legislative councils, elected representation and power over the budget.

s: Which of the following was an administrative demand of the Moderates?
o: Lowering the age limit for the ICS examination
Complete abolition of the civil services
Holding the ICS examination only in England
Separation of the judiciary from the executive
x: The Moderates demanded separation of the judiciary from the executive, along with simultaneous ICS examinations and a higher ICS age limit.

s: Separation of the judiciary from the executive was a Moderate demand of which kind?
x: It was among the administrative demands, with simultaneous ICS exams and Indianisation.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Moderates?
o: Their methods are summed up as prayers, petitions and protests
They sought to persuade the British public besides building opinion in India
They relied on mass civil disobedience to force the government
x: The Moderates used strictly constitutional agitation and distrusted mass action, so mass civil disobedience was not their method.

s: How long did the annual session of the INC generally last during the Moderate phase?
x: The annual session lasted only about three days, and the Congress had no effective machinery between sessions.

s: Which event most clearly exposed the Moderates' 'naive faith' in British justice?
o: establishment of the Indian Parliamentary Committee in 1893
appointment of the Welby Commission in 1895
formation of the British Committee in 1889
x: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 exposed the limitations of the Moderate faith in British justice and fair play.

s: Which leader opposed the Age of Consent Bill?
x: The Moderates generally supported the Age of Consent Bill, while Extremists such as Tilak opposed it.

s: What were the '3 Ps' of the Moderates' methods?
x: The Moderates relied on prayers, petitions and protests within strictly constitutional agitation.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Moderates:
1. They distrusted mass action.
2. The Congress had a standing machinery working between its annual sessions.
3. Their social base was narrow, urban and educated.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct; the Congress then had no machinery between sessions.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Book)
a. A Nation in the Making
b. Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
c. The Indian Struggle
d. The Man Who Divided India
List-II (Author)
1. Subhas Chandra Bose
2. Rafiq Zakaria
3. S.N. Banerjee
4. Dadabhai Naoroji
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: A Nation in the Making = S.N. Banerjee; Poverty and Un-British Rule = Naoroji; The Indian Struggle = Bose; The Man Who Divided India = Rafiq Zakaria.

s: Which Viceroy described the Congress as representing a 'microscopic minority'?
x: Dufferin used 'microscopic minority'; Curzon said it was 'tottering to its fall'.

s: In which year did Curzon write the letter in which he said the Congress was 'tottering to its fall'?
x: Curzon wrote it in a letter of 1900.

s: Who was the youngest Viceroy of India, appointed in 1899 at the age of 39?
x: Curzon became Viceroy in 1899 at 39, the youngest to hold the office.

s: Which of the following was NOT an achievement of the Moderate phase?
o: Development of a pan-Indian national identity
Training in parliamentary politics and civil liberties
x: The Moderates fostered national identity, economic critique and democratic training, but they did not achieve complete independence.

s: What did the Welby Commission, appointed in 1895, examine?
x: The Welby Commission of 1895 dealt with Indian expenditure and was regarded as one of the gains of Moderate pressure.

s: Why did the Congress find the Indian Councils Act of 1892 inadequate?
o: It abolished the legislative councils altogether
It gave no direct vote, kept an official majority and allowed the budget to be discussed but not amended
It gave Indians a majority in the councils but no say on the budget
It introduced separate electorates for Muslims
x: The INC called the 1892 Act inadequate because there was no direct vote, the councils kept an official majority, and the budget could only be discussed, not amended. It did not abolish councils, give Indians a majority, or create separate electorates.

s: Under which Viceroy was the Indian Councils Act of 1892 passed?
x: The Act was passed on 20 June 1892 under Lansdowne.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Indian Councils Act, 1892?
o: Members could vote on and amend the budget
x: Members could discuss the budget but could not vote on or amend it.

s: In which year was the British Committee of the INC formed in London?
x: The British Committee was formed in London in 1889, associated with Wedderburn and Naoroji; its journal was India.

s: Which journal was published by the British Committee of the INC (1889)?
x: The British Committee's journal was 'India' (1890); Voice of India was edited by Naoroji.

s: Who set up the Indian Parliamentary Committee in 1893 along with W.S. Caine?
x: William Wedderburn and W.S. Caine set up the Indian Parliamentary Committee (1893) to push for reforms in the House of Commons.

s: P. Anandacharlu, associated with the Moderate phase, presided over which session of the Indian National Congress?
x: P. Anandacharlu presided over the Nagpur Session of the Indian National Congress in 1891.

s: Who was the first Telugu President of the INC?
x: P. Anandacharlu, Secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884, was the first Telugu President of the INC.

s: Which region's annexation was opposed by the first session of the INC (1885)?
x: The 1885 session opposed the annexation of Upper Burma, while demanding simultaneous ICS exams, military cuts and elected councils.

s: Which Andhra delegate at the first INC session (Bombay, 1885) came from Rajahmundry?
x: Nyapathi Subbarao represented Rajahmundry; Anandacharlu was from Chittoor, Kesava Pillai from Gooty and Venkata Subbarayudu from Machilipatnam.

s: How many Andhra delegates attended the Madras session of the INC in 1914?
x: The Madras session of 1914 had 256 Andhra delegates.

s: Which of the following was NOT a demand of the first INC session (1885)?
o: Simultaneous ICS examinations in England and India
x: The first session opposed the annexation of Upper Burma; the other three were its demands.

s: Which session of the INC, held at Nagpur in 1891, was presided over by P. Anandacharlu?
x: P. Anandacharlu presided over the 7th session at Nagpur in 1891, the first Telugu President of the INC.

s: Which Andhra delegate at the first INC session (Bombay, 1885) came from Gooty?
x: Gutti Kesava Pillai came from Gooty; Anandacharlu from Chittoor, Nyapathi from Rajahmundry and Venkata Subbarayudu from Machilipatnam.

s: Of which body, founded in 1884, was P. Anandacharlu the secretary?
x: Anandacharlu was secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha (1884).

s: Who founded the Madras Native Association in 1852?
x: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty founded the Madras Native Association (26 February 1852) and was its first president.

s: In which year was the Madras Mahajana Sabha founded?
x: The Madras Mahajana Sabha was founded on 16 May 1884, with P. Rangaiah Naidu as president and P. Anandacharlu as secretary.

s: Who was the first secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha (1884)?
x: P. Anandacharlu was the secretary; P. Rangaiah Naidu was the president of the Sabha.

s: On the lines suggested at which of the following was the Krishna District Association formed?
o: First session of the Indian National Congress
Seventh session of the Indian National Congress
x: The Krishna District Association was formed on the lines suggested at the first session of the INC.

s: Which was the first district association in the Madras Presidency?
x: The Krishna District Association (1892) was the first in the Madras Presidency (APPSC-GS 2021); Vizag followed in 1893.

s: Which district association was formed in 1893?
x: Vizag District Association came in 1893, after Krishna (1892) and before Nellore (1908) and Kurnool (1914).

s: The youth of which town formed the Bala Bharathi Samiti in February 1907?
x: The Bala Bharathi Samiti was formed by the youth of Rajahmundry in February 1907, during Swadeshi.

s: Who founded the Godavari District Association at Rajahmundry in 1895?
x: Nyapathi Subbarao founded the Godavari District Association at Rajahmundry in 1895.

s: Which paper was founded as a result of an 1899 resolution of the Krishna District Association?
x: The Krishna District Association's 1899 resolution led to Krishna Patrika (1902).

s: Which pair of district association and founding year is correctly matched?
x: Nellore was founded in 1908; Vizag was 1893, Kurnool 1914 and Anantapur 1907.

s: Where was the second meeting of the Krishna District Association held in 1893?
x: The first meeting was at Guntur in July 1892; the second was at Machilipatnam in 1893.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Krishna District Association:
1. Its first meeting was held at Guntur in 1892.
2. It was formed on the lines suggested at the first session of the INC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: it was formed on the INC's suggestion and first met at Guntur in 1892.

s: Who presided over the Krishna District Association session of 1894?
x: Nyapathi Subbarao presided over the 1894 session and founded the Godavari District Association the next year.

s: Where was the first meeting of the Andhra Jana Sangam held on 14 February 1922?
x: The Andhra Jana Sangam held its first meeting at Hyderabad on 14 February 1922.

s: The Young Indian Association was formed after whose arrest?
x: The Young Indian Association was formed after the arrest of Annie Besant.

s: In which year was the Kurnool District Association formed?
x: The order of district bodies was Krishna 1892, Vizag 1893, Godavari 1895, Anantapur 1907, Nellore 1908 and Kurnool 1914.

s: Which monthly was founded by Nyapathi Subbarao?
x: Nyapathi Subbarao founded the monthly Vaijayanti and edited People's Magazine.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Andhra Prakasika — first political magazine in Andhra
Satyadoota — first political magazine in Andhra
Andhra Prakasika — first Telugu journal, run by the Bellary Christian mission
x: Andhra Prakasika was the first political magazine in Andhra (APPSC 2012). Satyadoota, run by the Bellary Christian mission, was the first Telugu journal, not a political magazine. Vyjayanti was Nyapathi Subbarao's monthly.

s: Who founded Krishna Patrika (1902) at Machilipatnam along with Konda Venkatappayya?
x: Krishna Patrika was founded on 2 February 1902 by Konda Venkatappayya and Dasu Narayana Rao; Mutnuri Krishna Rao edited it later.

s: Which Andhra leader brought out the monthly Vyjayanti?
x: Vyjayanti, a monthly, and the People's Magazine were associated with Nyapathi Subbarao.

s: About how many Telugu journals existed by 1905?
x: About 20 Telugu journals, such as Deshabhimani, Sasilekha and Gowtami, existed by 1905.

s: With which person is Andhra Prakasika correctly associated?
x: Andhra Prakasika, the first political magazine in Andhra, was a Telugu news weekly from Madras run by A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu. Pairing it with P. Anandacharyulu is the wrong pair (APPSC 2019 trap).

s: Who among the following later edited the Krishna Patrika, started at Machilipatnam in 1902?
x: Krishna Patrika was later edited by Mutnuri Krishna Rao, who made it a leading nationalist paper.

s: From which city was Andhra Prakasika, the first political magazine in Andhra, published?
x: Andhra Prakasika of A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu was a Telugu news weekly published from Madras.

s: Who was called the 'Father of South India'?
x: G. Subramania Iyer was the 'Father of South India'; Mocherla Ramachandra Rao was the 'Gokhale of South India'.

s: Who was described as the “Gokhale of South India”?
x: Mocherla Ramachandra Rao was described as the “Gokhale of South India.”

s: After 1908, which pair of Andhra Moderates came to the fore after the Extremists were crushed?
o: Gutti Kesava Pillai and Venkata Subbarayudu
Mocherla Ramachandra Rao and P. Rangaiah Naidu
x: After 1908, Konda Venkatappayya and B.N. Sarma came to the forefront among the Andhra Moderates.

s: In which year did Krishna Patrika first appear?
x: Krishna Patrika appeared in 1902, after the Madras Mahajana Sabha (1884), the first INC session (1885) and the Krishna District Association (1892).

s: Which body was founded first among these?
x: The Madras Mahajana Sabha (1884) came before the first INC (1885), the Krishna District Association (1892) and Krishna Patrika (1902).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Andhra spokesmen of the Moderate era?
o: P. Anandacharlu was secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha in 1884.
Nyapathi Subbarao founded the Godavari District Association.
P. Anandacharlu presented the data-led drain critique at the 7th Andhra Mahasabha, Guntur, 1919.
Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao critiqued the economic drain from Madras against Andhra in 1919.
x: The data-led drain critique at the 7th Andhra Mahasabha in Guntur (1919) was presented by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, not P. Anandacharlu.

s: Which Andhra spokesman held the titles 'Rajabahadur' and 'Padyavinoda'?
x: Nyapathi Subbarao, the Rajahmundry lawyer and Andhra spokesman, bore the titles Rajabahadur and Padyavinoda.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Moderates:
1. They repeated the INC's economic critique of the drain of wealth.
2. P. Anandacharlu attended the first INC session.
3. Nyapathi Subbarao was a Rajahmundry lawyer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: the Andhra Moderates echoed the drain critique, Anandacharlu attended the 1st INC, and Subbarao was a Rajahmundry lawyer.

s: How was the Andhras' opposition to the transfer of Ganjam to Orissa regarded?
x: The Andhra opposition to the transfer of Ganjam to Orissa was regarded as the first victory of the Andhra political movement.

s: In which year was Guntur district carved out of Krishna district?
x: Guntur district was carved from Krishna in 1904, and Konda Venkatappayya moved there.

s: Who was the leading municipal figure of Rajahmundry and founder of the Hindu Samaj there?
x: Nyapathi Subbarao led Rajahmundry's municipal politics and founded the Hindu Samaj there.

s: How was 16 October 1905, the day the partition of Bengal took effect, observed?
o: As a day of mourning, with hartal, Ganga bath and Rakhi-bandhan
With the founding of the National Council of Education
With the boycott resolution at Calcutta Town Hall
With the adoption of Swaraj by the Congress
x: 16 October 1905 was observed as a day of mourning and hartal; people bathed in the Ganga and tied rakhis as a symbol of unity.

s: In which year did leadership of the Swadeshi Movement pass from the Moderates to the Extremists?
x: The leadership of the movement passed from the Moderates to the Extremists in 1906.

s: On what did the Moderate campaign against the partition of Bengal (1903-1905) mainly rely?
x: The campaign led by S.N. Banerjee, K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray used petitions and meetings, and failed to prevent the partition.

s: Since which year has National Handloom Day been observed on 7 August?
x: National Handloom Day has been observed on 7 August since 2015, commemorating the Swadeshi proclamation at Calcutta Town Hall.

s: In which weekly did K.K. Mitra first suggest the boycott of British goods (13 July 1905)?
x: Krishna Kumar Mitra first suggested boycott in his weekly Sanjibani on 13 July 1905.

s: Who among the following led the Moderate campaign of petitions and meetings against the partition of Bengal (1903-05)?
x: S.N. Banerjee, with K.K. Mitra and Prithwishchandra Ray, led the Moderate campaign of petitions and meetings, which failed.

s: Which event occurred on 7 August 1905?
o: The partition of Bengal was annulled and the capital shifted to Delhi
The partition of Bengal formally took effect as a day of mourning
The boycott resolution was passed at Calcutta Town Hall and Swadeshi was formally proclaimed
The National Council of Education was established
x: On 7 August 1905, the boycott resolution was passed at Calcutta Town Hall and Swadeshi was formally proclaimed.

s: Who brought out the Bengali weekly 'Sanjibani'?
x: Sanjibani, a Bengali weekly of Calcutta, was started by Krishna Kumar Mitra.

s: The annulment of the partition of Bengal was announced at which event, and what important administrative change accompanied it?
o: The Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906; the capital was shifted from Delhi to Calcutta.
The Delhi Durbar of King George V in 1911; the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.
The Simla Conference of 1911; the capital was shifted from Delhi to Calcutta.
The Delhi Durbar of Edward VII in 1903; the capital was shifted from Calcutta to Bombay.
x: The partition was annulled on 12 December 1911 at the Delhi Durbar of King George V. The capital was simultaneously transferred from Calcutta to Delhi.

s: Who described Bengal as “the nerve centre of Indian nationalism” in the context of the partition of Bengal?
x: Lord Curzon described Bengal as “the nerve centre of Indian nationalism,” reflecting the political significance he attached to the province.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: King George V — Viceroy who announced the partition of Bengal
Lord Hardinge II — Viceroy at the time of annulment
H.H. Risley — “Bengal united is a power”
x: King George V was the monarch at whose Delhi Durbar the annulment was announced; he was not the Viceroy who announced the partition. Lord Curzon announced the partition, while Lord Hardinge II was Viceroy at the time of its annulment.

s: Which event helped intensify anger against the partition of Bengal?
o: The formation of the Muslim League in 1909
x: Japan’s victory over Russia in 1904–05 inspired Asian and Indian nationalist sentiment and fed anger against the partition (Sumit Sarkar's interpretation).

s: What was the official justification given for the partition of Bengal?
x: Administrative convenience was the stated reason; the real aim was to weaken Bengali nationalism and divide Hindus and Muslims.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: The Partition of Bengal was announced in 1905.
The partition became effective on 15 October 1905.
Lord Curzon was the Viceroy associated with the partition.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Partition of Bengal took effect on 16 October 1905, not 15 October. It was announced in 1905 under Lord Curzon and annulled in 1911.

s: Which was the capital of the new province of Eastern Bengal and Assam (1905)?
x: Eastern Bengal and Assam had Dacca as its capital, while Western Bengal kept Calcutta.

s: Who said, 'Bengal united is a power; Bengal divided will pull in several different ways'?
x: Home Secretary H.H. Risley made this remark, revealing the real motive of weakening Bengali nationalism.

s: Who was the Viceroy when the partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911?
x: Lord Hardinge II was Viceroy at the 1911 Delhi Durbar of George V; Curzon had carried out the partition.

s: Whose coronation did the Delhi Durbar of 1903 celebrate?
x: The 1903 Durbar celebrated Edward VII's coronation; the 1911 Durbar of George V annulled the partition.

s: After the partition of 1905, the rest of Bengal had a population of 54 million. Which of the following was true of it?
x: Of 54 million, only 18 million were Bengalis against 36 million Biharis and Oriyas, so Bengalis became a minority in their own province.

s: With reference to the Partition of Bengal, which pair is correctly matched?
x: The partition was announced in 1905 by Viceroy Lord Curzon; the major response was the Swadeshi Movement and nationalists saw it as 'Divide and Rule'.

s: Which Delhi Durbar was the only one attended by the reigning British sovereign?
x: The 1911 Durbar, which annulled the partition, was the only Durbar a sovereign attended in person.

s: Who said that the Partition of Bengal 'fell on us like a bomb'?
x: Surendranath Banerjee said the 1905 Partition of Bengal fell on them like a bomb.

s: Against what did S.G. Deuskar write 'Desher Katha' chiefly to warn Indians?
o: the use of Indian languages in administration
the decline of Sanskrit education under the Mughals
the division of Bengal into linguistic provinces
the British ‘hypnotic conquest of the mind’
x: S.G. Deuskar’s ‘Desher Katha’ warned against the British ‘hypnotic conquest of the mind’.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee wrote ‘Bande Mataram’, which became the anthem of the Swadeshi movement. ‘Desher Katha’ was written by S.G. Deuskar.

s: Who painted 'Bharat Mata' (1905)?
x: Abanindranath Tagore painted Bharat Mata in 1905.

s: Who founded the Indian Society of Oriental Art (1907) along with Abanindranath Tagore?
x: Abanindranath and Gaganendranath Tagore founded the Indian Society of Oriental Art (1907) of the Bengal School.

s: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: Amar Sonar Bangla – Bankim Chandra Chatterjee
x: Desher Katha (1904) is by S.G. Deuskar; Bande Mataram is Bankim's, Amar Sonar Bangla Tagore's and Hindu Desa Daridryam Attili Suryanarayana Rao's.

s: In which novel did Rabindranath Tagore show his dislike of the economic side of the Swadeshi movement?
x: Tagore disliked the economic side of Swadeshi, shown in his novel Ghare Baire.

s: Who was the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize?
x: Tagore won the Nobel Prize for Literature for Song Offerings (Gitanjali), the first Asian to win it.

s: Which artist led the illumination of the original handwritten manuscript of the Constitution of India?
x: Nandalal Bose of the Bengal School and his Santiniketan students illustrated the original Constitution; Prem Behari Narain Raizada did the calligraphy.

s: Which painter set up a lithographic press at Bombay in 1894 to print his pictures of gods and epics?
x: Raja Ravi Varma of Kilimanoor set up the Ravi Varma Fine Art Lithographic Press at Bombay in 1894.

s: The Swadeshi movement of 1905 is regarded as the first movement of which kind in India?
x: The Swadeshi movement was regarded as the first mass movement and marked the birth of mass nationalism.

s: What was the principal feature of the Swadeshi and Boycott movement during the period of the Partition of Bengal?
o: Boycott foreign goods and promote indigenous goods and national education
Accept the Nehru Report and begin a mass movement
Adopt Complete Independence as the Congress goal
Draft a constitutional framework for India
x: The Swadeshi and Boycott movement against the 1905 Partition of Bengal boycotted foreign goods and promoted Indian goods and national education. Complete Independence and the Nehru Report came in the late 1920s.

s: For what purpose were jatras, melas, akharas and lathi clubs used during the Swadeshi Movement?
x: Jatras, folk songs, melas, volunteer corps, akharas and lathi clubs were all used for mass mobilisation.

s: Besides foreign cloth and foreign salt, which foreign item was a principal target of the Swadeshi boycott?
x: The boycott targeted foreign cloth, salt and sugar, while indigenous handloom goods were encouraged.

s: The Swadesh Bandhab Samiti of Barisal used which of these?
x: Ashwini Kumar Dutt's Swadesh Bandhab Samiti used magic lanterns, social work and arbitration courts.

s: Who presided over the Calcutta session of the INC (1906), which declared Swaraj the goal?
x: Dadabhai Naoroji presided at Calcutta (1906), where resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education were passed.

s: The Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company was associated with which of the following persons and places?
x: V.O. Chidambaram Pillai established the Swadeshi Steam Navigation Company at Tuticorin in 1906.

s: Who was the first principal of Bengal National College?
x: Aurobindo Ghosh served as the first principal of Bengal National College.

s: How were the Banga Lakshmi Cotton Mills set up in 1906?
x: Banga Lakshmi Cotton Mills (1906) were set up by public subscription; P.C. Ray founded Bengal Chemical Swadeshi Stores.

s: Which Swadeshi bank was founded in 1907?
x: Among Swadeshi banks, Bank of India came in 1906 and Indian Bank in 1907.

s: Which university grew out of the National Council of Education set up on 15 August 1906?
x: The National Council of Education (1906) later became Jadavpur University.

s: In which year did Tilak start the Shivaji festival?
x: Tilak began Ganeshotsav in 1893 and the Shivaji festival in 1895.

s: Which one of the following regional associations is correctly matched?
o: Bengal — Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal and Ashwini Kumar Dutt
Punjab — V.O. Chidambaram Pillai and Ajit Singh
Madras — Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Syed Haider Raza
Delhi — Konda Venkatappayya and C.Y. Chintamani
x: Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal and Ashwini Kumar Dutt were associated with Bengal. The other options combine leaders from different regions.

s: Who founded Bengal Chemicals during the Swadeshi Movement?
x: Bengal Chemicals was founded by Acharya P.C. Ray as a Swadeshi enterprise.

s: Which leader of the Extremist era was associated with Delhi?
x: Syed Haider Raza led in Delhi; Ashwini Kumar Dutt was in Bengal, Chidambaram Pillai in Madras and Lajpat Rai in Punjab.

x: The Andhra Jateeya Kalasala (National College) at Machilipatnam was started in 1910 as part of the national education movement.

s: How did the Extremists compare with the Moderates on social reform?
x: The Moderates were generally pro-reform while the Extremists were comparatively orthodox; Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill.

s: Which bill did Tilak oppose, showing the Extremists' comparatively orthodox stand on social reform?
x: Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill; the Extremists were comparatively orthodox on social reform.

s: On which date was Tilak's Home Rule League founded?
x: Tilak began his league on 28 April 1916; Besant's followed in September 1916.

s: Where was Tilak imprisoned for six years after his 1908 sedition trial?
x: Tilak got six years in Mandalay in 1908, after 18 months in 1897; he was acquitted in 1916.

s: Which one of the following newspapers was published by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in Marathi?
x: Tilak published Kesari in Marathi and Mahratta in English; both newspapers began in 1881.

s: In which year did Tilak start the public Ganesh Utsav?
x: Tilak made Ganesh Utsav a public festival in 1893 and Shivaji Jayanti in 1895.

s: In which year did Bal Gangadhar Tilak join the Indian National Congress?
x: Tilak joined the Congress in 1890; he founded his Home Rule League on 28 April 1916.

s: In which year did Tilak revive Shivaji Jayanti as a public festival?
x: Shivaji Jayanti began in 1895; public Ganesh Utsav was started earlier, in 1893.

s: In which year was Tilak released from Mandalay jail?
x: Tilak was released on 16 June 1914, not 1916.

s: What sentence did Tilak receive in his first sedition trial of 1897?
x: In 1897 Tilak got 18 months; the six-year sentence at Mandalay came in 1908.

s: Who was the president of Tilak's Home Rule League (1916)?
x: Tilak's Home Rule League of 28 April 1916 had Joseph Baptista as president; Besant's League came in September 1916.

s: In June 1897, the Chapekar brothers killed which Plague Committee official at Poona?
x: The Chapekar brothers killed Rand (and Lt Ayerst) in June 1897, and Tilak was accused of conspiracy.

s: Who is the author of 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas'?
x: Tilak wrote 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas', placing the Aryan homeland in the Arctic; he also wrote Gita Rahasya.

s: Where was Bal Gangadhar Tilak born in 1856?
x: Tilak was born on 23 July 1856 at Ratnagiri in Maharashtra.

s: With whom did Tilak found the Deccan Education Society, which set up Fergusson College?
x: Tilak and Agarkar started the New English School and the Deccan Education Society, which founded Fergusson College.

s: Which European scholar pleaded for Tilak after his sedition sentence of 1897?
x: Max Muller pleaded for Tilak in 1897, saying his interest in Tilak was that of a Sanskrit scholar.

s: In which year did Bal Gangadhar Tilak die?
x: Tilak died on 1 August 1920; Gandhi, Shaukat Ali and Saifuddin Kitchlew lifted his bier.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gita Rahasya — written by Tilak in Mandalay
The Soul of India — Aurobindo Ghosh
x: Tilak wrote Gita Rahasya while imprisoned in Mandalay. New India (the renamed Madras Standard) was Annie Besant's paper, The Punjabee was Lajpat Rai's, and The Soul of India was written by Bipin Chandra Pal.

s:
Consider the following statements about Tilak's newspapers:
1. Kesari was published in Marathi.
2. Mahratta was published in English.
3. Both were started in 1881.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct: Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English) were both started in 1881.

s: Which newspaper is associated with Bal Gangadhar Tilak?
x: Kesari is linked with Tilak, along with the Ganpati Festival and Gita Rahasya.

s: At which place was Bal Gangadhar Tilak imprisoned for six years?
x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak served a six-year imprisonment at Mandalay.

s: The British journalist Valentine Chirol called which leader the Father of Indian Unrest?
x: Chirol called Bal Gangadhar Tilak (Lokmanya, of Maharashtra) the Father of Indian Unrest. Pal led in Bengal, Lajpat Rai in Punjab (Punjab Kesari), and Aurobindo edited Bande Mataram.

s: Where was Bal Gangadhar Tilak born in 1856?
x: Tilak was born on 23 July 1856 at Ratnagiri.

s: What was the main objective of the Extremists or Assertive Nationalists?
o: Swaraj or complete independence from English rule
x: The Extremists, or Assertive Nationalists, aimed at Swaraj, meaning complete independence from British rule. Constitutional agitation, negotiation and gradual self-government were Moderate ideas.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Moderates were associated with the period 1885–1905.
Moderates sought more immediate Swaraj than the Extremists.
Extremists showed increasing distrust of British rule.
Extremists favoured agitation and mass mobilisation.
x: Option B is incorrect: the Moderates wanted gradual reform through petitions, while the Extremists demanded more immediate Swaraj. The Moderate phase was 1885–1905, and the Extremists distrusted British rule and used agitation.

s: Which of the following statements regarding the methods of the Extremists is incorrect?
o: They accepted Prayer, Petition and Protest as their principal method.
x: Option A is incorrect: the Extremists rejected Prayer, Petition and Protest, which was the Moderate method. They favoured self-sacrifice, mass movement and aggressive resistance.

s: What was the aim of the Moderates?
x: The Moderates sought gradual self-government through constitutional agitation; the Extremists sought Swaraj.

s: Which pair consists only of representative Moderate leaders?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh
x: Dadabhai Naoroji and Gopal Krishna Gokhale were both Moderates. Tilak, Lajpat Rai, Bipin Chandra Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh were Extremists, so every other pair includes an Extremist.

s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
x: The Maharashtra extremist group was led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak; Bengal was associated with Pal and Aurobindo, and Punjab with Lala Lajpat Rai.

s: Which of the following was a criticism of Extremist politics?
o: Its religious symbolism alienated Muslims and its social outlook was orthodox.
It weakened the demand for Swaraj by supporting colonial rule.
It completely rejected all cultural symbols.
It prevented the use of boycott and Swadeshi.
x: The Extremists were criticised for using religious symbolism that alienated Muslims and for being socially orthodox. The Surat Split was also regarded as weakening the Congress.

s: The '3 Ss' method – self-reliance, self-sacrifice and strong will – belonged to which group?
x: The 3 Ss were the Extremists' method; the 3 Ps (prayers, petitions, protests) were the Moderates'.

s: What did 'Atmashakti' mean in Extremist ideology?
x: Atmashakti meant self-reliance. It was connected with constructive work such as the establishment of cooperatives.

s: What was the main contribution of the Extremists to the national movement?
o: turning nationalism into a mass movement and making Swaraj its goal
supporting permanent British control over India
restricting nationalism to educated constitutional petitioners
x: The Extremists broadened nationalism into a mass movement and placed Swaraj at the centre of the political goal.

s: Which one of the following was NOT a method associated with extremist nationalism?
x: The Extremists had no faith in British generosity. Their methods included passive resistance, mass agitation, boycott, Swadeshi, national education and self-sacrifice.

s: How did spiritual nationalism view the nation?
x: Spiritual nationalism represented the nation as a mother goddess, an idea expressed through symbols such as Bande Mataram and Bhavani Mandir.

s: Aurobindo set out the doctrine of passive resistance in which paper?
x: Aurobindo set out passive resistance in Bande Mataram; Indu Prakash carried his earlier New Lamps for Old.

s: What did Swaraj mean for the Extremists?
o: Colonial self-government within the British Empire
x: Extremist Swaraj meant complete freedom, not colonial self-government, pursued through boycott, Swadeshi, national education and passive resistance.

s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Lal refers to Lala Lajpat Rai.
Pal refers to Bipin Chandra Pal.
The trio included Aurobindo Ghosh instead of Bipin Chandra Pal.
Bal refers to Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
x: Option C is incorrect: the Lal–Bal–Pal trio was Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal. Aurobindo Ghosh is added only in the longer group Lal–Bal–Pal–Ghosh.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: Lajpat Rai led the Extremists in Punjab. Tilak led in Maharashtra, Pal in Bengal and V.O. Chidambaram Pillai in the Madras Presidency.

s: Which leader was NOT part of the trio Lal-Bal-Pal?
x: Lal-Bal-Pal were Lajpat Rai, Tilak and Pal; Aurobindo appears only in 'Lal-Bal-Pal-Ghosh'.

s: Which group wanted to extend the Swadeshi-Boycott movement more widely?
o: The British Committee of the INC
x: It was the Extremists who wanted to widen the Swadeshi-Boycott movement; the Moderates were reluctant.

s: By 1910, with Tilak in jail and Aurobindo retired, which group came to dominate the Congress?
x: By 1910 Tilak was in jail, Aurobindo had retired, Pal had been arrested and Lajpat Rai had left, enabling the Moderates to dominate the Congress.

s: Who presided over the Benaras session of the Indian National Congress in 1905?
x: Gokhale became Congress President at 39 at the Benaras session of 1905.

s: The immediate cause of the Surat Split of 1907 was chiefly the dispute between Moderates and Extremists over:
o: the annulment of the partition of Bengal
the formation of the Muslim League
the four resolutions adopted at Calcutta
x: The Surat clash centred on the four resolutions passed at Calcutta in 1906 (Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education): the Extremists wanted them kept and the boycott extended to all India, while the Moderates wanted them dropped. Separate electorates, the annulment of partition (1911) and the Muslim League were not the issue.

s: What was the immediate outcome of the Surat session of 1907?
o: The Moderates pushed out the Extremists and the session was suspended
x: The Moderates, being in a majority, pushed out the Extremists; a scuffle followed and the session was suspended.

s: Who led the Moderates at the Surat session of 1907?
x: Gokhale and Pherozeshah Mehta led the Moderates (Naram Dal) at Surat; Tilak led the Extremists.

s: Who presided over the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906?
x: Dadabhai Naoroji presided at Calcutta in 1906, where a split was averted and the four resolutions were passed.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Calcutta session of the INC, 1906:
1. It was presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji.
2. It passed resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education.
3. The Congress split into two wings at this session.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Naoroji presided and the four resolutions were passed at Calcutta; the split came a year later at Surat (1907).

s: At the Surat session of 1907, which group was called the 'Garam Dal'?
x: The Extremists led by Tilak were the Garam Dal; the Moderates led by Gokhale and Mehta were the Naram Dal.

s: Which one of the following Acts was enacted in 1908 to deal with incitement to offences through newspapers?
x: The Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act was enacted in 1908. The Indian Press Act followed in 1910.

s: In which year was the Indian Press Act enacted?
x: The Indian Press Act was enacted in 1910, following the Newspapers (Incitement to Offences) Act of 1908.

s: In which year was the Seditious Meetings Act passed?
x: The Seditious Meetings Act came in 1907; the Newspapers Act in 1908 and the Indian Press Act in 1910.

s: Which two leaders were deported in 1908?
o: Ashwini Kumar Dutt and K.K. Mitra
x: Ashwini Kumar Dutt and K.K. Mitra were deported in 1908; Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh had been deported in 1907.

s: Who was known as 'Andhra Tilak'?
x: Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao, called Andhra Tilak, was jailed in 1908.

s: Which pair of repressive Act and year is correctly matched?
x: The Explosive Substances Act was of 1908; Seditious Meetings 1907, Newspapers Act 1908, Indian Press Act 1910.

s: Where did the Moderates and Extremists reunite after the Surat Split?
x: The reunion came at Lucknow in 1916, not in 1908; the split was followed by repression, the Newspapers Act of 1908 and Tilak's imprisonment.

s: Which of the following sets of resolutions was associated with the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906?
o: Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education
Separate electorates, provincial autonomy, adult franchise and federation
Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Quit India and Khilafat
Council entry, constitutional reform, Home Rule and communal award
x: The Calcutta session of 1906 passed resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education as a compromise between Moderates and Extremists.

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Surat Split
B. Lucknow Pact
C. Swadeshi Movement
D. Morley-Minto Reforms
x: The sequence is Swadeshi Movement in 1905, Surat Split in 1907, Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and Lucknow Pact in 1916.

s: Which one of the following events took place in 1911?
o: The Partition of Bengal was annulled
The Tilak Home Rule League was founded
x: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911. Tilak was released in 1914, the Lucknow Pact was concluded in 1916, and the Tilak Home Rule League began in 1916.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the order of these events?
o: The INC was founded before the partition of Bengal
The Muslim League was formed after the partition of Bengal
The Muslim League was formed before the founding of the INC
The Surat Split came after the formation of the Muslim League
x: INC 1885, partition 1905, Muslim League 1906, Surat Split 1907, so the League came after the INC, not before.

s: Which of the following did NOT take place during the Extremist phase of the national movement?
x: The Swadeshi Movement (1905), Surat Split (1907) and Tilak's Mandalay sentence (1908) fall in the Extremist phase; the Lucknow Pact (1916) came later.

s: Who was the Moderate nominee for president at the Surat session (1907)?
x: Rash Behari Ghosh was the Moderate nominee; the Extremists wanted Tilak or Lajpat Rai.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Surat Split:
1. The Extremists wanted the session at Nagpur.
2. Minto called it 'a great triumph for us'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the session was moved from Nagpur to Surat, and Minto welcomed the split as a great triumph.

s: Which of the following belongs to the Extremist phase of the national movement?
x: The Swadeshi movement and the Surat Split (1907) are of the Extremist phase; Morley-Minto was a government response and Home Rule and the Lucknow Pact were the reunion phase.

s: Who set up the Indian Home Rule League of America in 1917?
x: Lajpat Rai went to the USA after 1908 and founded the Indian Home Rule League of America (1917).

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal — The Arctic Home in the Vedas
x: Lala Lajpat Rai was associated with The Punjabee. The Arctic Home in the Vedas was written by Tilak, Unhappy India by Lajpat Rai and The Soul of India by Pal.

s: Which of the following statements about Lala Lajpat Rai is incorrect?
o: He was known as Sher-e-Punjab and Punjab Kesari.
He died on 17 November 1928 after the Maniktalla Garden raid.
He was a member of the Lal–Bal–Pal trio.
x: Option B is incorrect: Lajpat Rai died on 17 November 1928 from lathi injuries suffered during the Simon Commission protest at Lahore. The Maniktalla Garden raid is linked with Aurobindo Ghosh.

s: In which year did Lala Lajpat Rai start 'Young India' in the USA?
x: Young India was started in the USA in 1916; the Indian Home Rule League of America followed in 1917.

s: When did Lala Lajpat Rai die?
x: Lajpat Rai died on 17 November 1928 after the lathi-charge at Lahore during the anti-Simon protest.

s: Who is the author of 'The Story of My Deportation' (1908)?
x: Lajpat Rai wrote The Story of My Deportation after he was deported to Mandalay in 1907.

s: In which city was Lala Lajpat Rai fatally injured in a lathi-charge during the protest against the Simon Commission?
x: Lajpat Rai led the 'Go back Simon' protest at Lahore, was hurt in the lathi-charge and died on 17 November 1928.

s: Which one of the following slogans is associated with Lala Lajpat Rai?
o: Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it
x: Lala Lajpat Rai is associated with the slogan ‘Go back Simon’. Tilak’s slogan was ‘Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it’.

s: Which Extremist leader was known as 'Punjab Kesari'?
x: Lala Lajpat Rai was called Punjab Kesari and Sher-e-Punjab.

s: In which year was Lala Lajpat Rai deported by the British?
x: Lajpat Rai was deported in 1907; Tilak was sent to Mandalay in 1908.

s: In 1907, Lala Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported to Mandalay under which law?
x: They were deported to Mandalay in 1907 under Regulation III of 1818. The Defence of India Act came only in 1915 and the Rowlatt Act in 1919, so neither could apply in 1907; the Press Act was a press law, not a deportation law.

s:
Consider the following statements about Aurobindo Ghosh:
1. He edited Bande Mataram.
2. He was convicted in the Alipore case.
3. He retired to Pondicherry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Aurobindo edited Bande Mataram and retired to Pondicherry; he was acquitted, not convicted, in the Alipore case.

s: Which one of the following was regarded as the chief ideologue of the Extremists?
x: Aurobindo Ghosh was regarded as the chief ideologue of the Extremist wing.

s: Who was called the 'Prophet of Indian Nationalism'?
x: Aurobindo Ghosh is called the Prophet of Indian Nationalism.

s: Who was called the 'Father of Revolutionary Thoughts'?
x: Bipin Chandra Pal was called the Father of Revolutionary Thoughts.

s: Who co-edited Bande Mataram with Aurobindo Ghosh?
x: Bipin Chandra Pal is identified with Aurobindo Ghosh as a co-editor of Bande Mataram.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal — deported to Mandalay in 1907
Ashwini Kumar Dutt and K.K. Mitra — Bengal leaders deported in 1908
Bal Gangadhar Tilak — sent to Mandalay in 1908
Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh — deported in 1907
x: Bipin Chandra Pal was arrested in 1907 for refusing to testify in the Bande Mataram case; he was not deported to Mandalay. Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh were deported in 1907, while Tilak and the mentioned Bengal leaders faced repression in 1908.

s: Who founded the weekly 'New India' in 1901?
x: Bipin Chandra Pal founded New India (1901).

s: Bipin Chandra Pal was a member of which of the following?
x: Pal belonged to the Brahmo Samaj; Lajpat Rai was the Arya Samaj leader.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Bipin Chandra Pal?
o: He was deported to Mandalay in 1907
He started the weekly New India in 1901
He lived in England from 1908 to 1911
x: Pal was arrested in 1907 for refusing to testify in the Bande Mataram case, not deported; Lajpat Rai was deported to Mandalay.

s: Who wrote 'The Soul of India'?
x: The Soul of India was written by Bipin Chandra Pal, who also started the weekly New India in 1901.

s: In which year did Aurobindo retire to Pondicherry?
x: Aurobindo retired to Pondicherry in 1910, after his acquittal in the Alipore case in 1909.

s: In which journal did Aurobindo's 'New Lamps for Old' appear?
x: New Lamps for Old (1893-94) was a series of nine articles in Indu Prakash, Bombay.

s: Of which institution was Aurobindo Ghosh the first principal?
x: Aurobindo was the first principal of Bengal National College.
